note: Rewritten from the species description in Scheffrahn & Pinzón Florian (2020), originally in English; the alate is only 1 damaged female and the soldier sample is n=6, measurements as in the original; the text omits type material, locality, distribution and ecology, and plate information is not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is the only drywood termite known worldwide with a dark anterior part of the head capsule that is not of the explosive (dehiscent) type, so its head colour alone separates it from all congeners; moreover the outer corners of the anterolateral ridges project forward as acute angles (right or obtuse in other South American, Central American and Australasian Rugitermes). The alate has a black head capsule and a brown-orange pronotum, similar in colour to R. bicolor, R. flavicinctus, R. magninotus and R. nodulosus: R. bicolor is larger, R. flavicinctus smaller, R. magninotus has a brown head and a yellow pronotum, while the species treated here has a black head and a brown pronotum; R. nodulosus is known only from Minas Gerais, southern Brazil.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Only one damaged female: the distal half of the left wing is torn and the right wing is missing. Head capsule black, pronotum orange brown; compound eyes small, nearly circular; ocelli minute, circular, black, difficult to discern because they do not contrast with the head capsule, far from the eye margin. Vertex and frons not concave, frons with shallow rugae, bearing several dozen erect setae about 0.15 mm long. Pronotum slightly wider than the head capsule, anterior margin shallowly concave, posterolateral corners evenly rounded, posterior margin narrowly concave, pilosity as on the vertex. Antenna with at least 16 segments, relative lengths of the basal segments 1>2=3>4. Anterior half of the forewing as in the genus, the media very short, merging with the radius 0.9 mm from the wing scale; wing scale with about 20 setae; wing membrane smoky brown, with dark tubercles. Legs dark brown; arolium present.
Measurements (mm, maximum values): head width 1.31, pronotum width 1.43, compound eye diameter 0.32, ocellus diameter 0.01, body length 7.9.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head capsule dark chestnut brown in dorsal view from the posterior margin of the postclypeus to the posterior quarter, the posterior quarter grading from dark reddish brown to orange brown on the occiput; in ventral view the head capsule grades from dark chestnut brown to orange brown, only the posterior part of the postmentum remaining dark reddish brown. Pronotum yellow with a reddish interior, in marked contrast to the head colour. Head capsule long, rectangular, lateral margins slightly concave medially, sparsely setose except on the more densely setose frons. Pronotum much wider than long, setae scattered and denser on the lateral margins, anterior margin weakly concave. In dorsal view the frontal margin forms a weakly hemispherical rim around the frons, at about 30° to the plane of the vertex; frons finely rugose. Anterolateral ridges forming platforms on either side of the frons that are nearly level with the posterior margin of the postclypeus, their outer edge with an acute projection of about 65°; in frontal view the ridge is slightly raised at the projection, and the dorsal edge of the antennal ridges (antennal sockets) is distinctly lower than the ridge. Eye spots small, concolorous with the head capsule. Third antennal segment club-shaped, about twice as long as the second and fourth segments. Mandibles about half the length of the head capsule, outer edge gradually curved, base slightly swollen.
Measurements (mm, mean (range, n=6)): head length to lateral mandible base 2.83 (2.47—2.99), maximum head width 1.72 (1.52—1.90), head height including postmentum 1.42 (1.29—1.47), maximum pronotum width 1.86 (1.58—2.04), maximum pronotum length 0.90 (0.86—0.95), third antennal segment length 0.19 (0.18—0.20).
